author: rdc-rfc1-author-b (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: Two resets are each synchronised on clk, ANDed and registered, so the exported reset is glitch-free and releases on clk. acc_rst_q's D is low at por_ni release.

author_reading.rationale: Two independently synchronised resets are combined in one domain and registered, so the accelerator reset is a single clock-edge-driven signal.

labels.rationale: Both resets pass through their own 2-stage synchronisers on clk, and acc_rst_q registers their AND on clk. The output changes only at clock edges, so the combined reset is safe.
Debug reset can asynchronously clear dbg_sync_q[1] while acc_rst_q stays active. The D transition can meet the acc_rst_q aperture and propagate metastability onto the exported reset.
labels.suspected_flaw: The output flop samples asynchronous assertion of the independently reset debug stage. No accelerator receiver is present.

settlement.rationale: A is right. B's hazard is a debug-reset assertion reaching acc_rst_q's D asynchronously. At worst that delays or briefly blurs an assertion that settles to asserted on the next edge, and corrupts no state; the registered output is the standard remedy for combining resets. RDC-004 may still report it as an obligation.
